newsitem.title: USA: Komag sees weak results for rest of year.
newsitem.headline: Komag sees weak results for rest of year.

text.p: Komag Inc. warned Wednesday that results for its second quarter and the rest of its fiscal year would fall short of expectations due to weak demand for disk drives.

The San Jose-based company said in a statement that earnings for its second quarter, ending June 29, will be below the $0.33 a share it earned in its first quarter. Komag said sales would be slightly higher than the $167.2 million of revenues it had in the first quarter.
Analysts had expected the company to earn 45 cents a share in the second quarter, according to First Call. In the comparable year-ago quarter Komag had profits of $42.5 million, or 80 cents a share.

The company, which makes thin-film media for computer hard disk drives, attributed the shortfall to weak demand for very large disk drives and lower than expected production levels. Komag said second quarter gross margins will fall slightly below the 23.5 percent reported for the first quarter. It also said its 50 percent-owned Japanese joint venture, Asahi Komag Company Ltd., will post a second quarter loss due to product transitions.

Orders from Seagate Technology Inc., the biggest disk drive maker in the world, will be cut in half to about 15 percent of sales compared to the first quarter, Komag said. The company had expected Seagate's orders to rise for the rest of the fiscal year.

The company said because of the lower Seagate orders it will have excess production capacity which will cause gross margins and earnings for the third and fourth fiscal quarter to fall below first and second quarter levels. Komag is reviewing its plans to spend $290 million for capital expenditures during fiscal 1997 in light of the weaker results.
